curve-analysis__ca-concavity__mcq.A curve has f′ < 0 and f″ > 0. What is i: Falling, but the fall is levelling off — bending back upward.

curve-analysis__ca-critical-point__mcq.Why does the definition include 'f′ does: Because |x| has a minimum at its corner, where f′ does not exist at all.

curve-analysis__ca-evt__mcq.Why does f(x) = x on the OPEN interval (: It climbs all the way to 1 but never reaches it — the endpoint is not included.

curve-analysis__ca-first-derivative-test.f′ is positive on (−∞, −2), negative on: On (−2, 2) — the interval where f′ is negative.

curve-analysis__ca-inflection__mcq.What makes x = c an inflection point?: f″ CHANGES SIGN at c — the bend switches direction.
curve-analysis__ca-inflection__mcq.f(x) = x⁴ has f″(0) = 0. Is x = 0 an inf: No — f″ = 12x² is positive on BOTH sides, so the bend never changes.

curve-analysis__ca-mvt-consequences__mcq.f′(x) = 0 for every x. What follows, and: f is constant — the MVT forces f(x₂) − f(x₁) = 0·(x₂ − x₁) = 0 for any two points.
curve-analysis__ca-mvt-consequences__mcq.Why is every antiderivative of f of the: Two antiderivatives have the same derivative, so their difference has derivative 0 — and the MVT says that makes it constant.

curve-analysis__ca-optimisation-applied_.A profit function P(x) has P′(x) > 0 for: At x = 40 — the right endpoint. Profit is still climbing when the range runs out.

Put an optimisation problem in the right: Write a formula for the quantity to be optimised
Use the constraint to reduce it to ONE variable
Differentiate, and compare critical points with the endpoints

curve-analysis__ca-read-f-prime__mcq.The graph of f′ has a MAXIMUM at x = 1 (: An inflection point — and the steepest climb of f.

curve-analysis__ca-rolle__mcq.f(x) = |x| − 1 on [−1, 1] has f(−1) = f(: Differentiability — there is a corner at x = 0.

curve-analysis__ca-second-derivative-tes.f′(c) = 0 and f″(c) = 0. What can you co: Nothing — use the sign chart of f′ instead.
curve-analysis__ca-second-derivative-tes.f has a critical point at a CORNER, wher: The first-derivative test — look at the sign of f′ on either side.

curve-analysis__ca-three-charts__mcq.For f = x⁴ − 4x³, x = 0 is a critical po: A saddle AND an inflection point — the two charts describe different things.
curve-analysis__ca-three-charts__mcq.On an interval, f′ > 0 and f″ < 0. What: Rising, but levelling off — heading toward a maximum.

derivative-rules__dr-chain-nested__mcq.How many factors will the derivative of: Three — one for the root, one for the cube, one for the bracket.

derivative-rules__dr-derivative-function.You traced f′ for f(x) = x². What kind o: A function — one slope for each input, here f′(x) = 2x.

derivative-rules__dr-differentiability__.|x| is continuous at x = 0 but has no de: Continuity is necessary for differentiability, but not sufficient.

derivative-rules__dr-flat-not-turning__m.For f(x) = x³, f′(0) = 0. Does f have a: Neither — it flattens and keeps climbing. f′ never changes sign.

derivative-rules__dr-implicit-practice__.On x² + y² = 25, why does dy/dx = −x/y d: Because the curve has two points above most x-values, with opposite slopes — and only y can distinguish them.

derivative-rules__dr-local-linearity__mc.You magnify a graph at a point and it be: f is differentiable there — locally straight is what having a derivative looks like.

derivative-rules__dr-trig-derivative__mc.Why does (cos x)′ = −sin x carry a minus: Just past x = 0 the cosine is falling, so its derivative must be negative — and sin x is positive there.

derivatives-in-context__dc-choosing-rela.A person walks away from a lamppost; the: Similar triangles — the lamp/person/shadow makes two triangles of the same shape.
derivatives-in-context__dc-choosing-rela.V = (1/3)πr²h, and the cone's shape forc: V = (1/12)πh³ — substitute r = h/2 FIRST, so only h remains.

derivatives-in-context__dc-differentials.A quantity s is measured with a 4% error: About 2% — the exponent is 1/2, so the relative error is halved.

derivatives-in-context__dc-lhopital__mcq.lim(x→0) (x² + 1)/(x + 1). A student app: The form is not indeterminate — substitution gives 1/1 = 1. L'Hôpital does not apply, and using it produced a wrong answer.

derivatives-in-context__dc-linearisation.Two curves are linearised at the same po: The one with |f″| = 0.01 — it is nearly straight already.
derivatives-in-context__dc-linearisation.Why can f(x) = |x| not be linearised at: f′(0) does not exist — there is no tangent line, so there is nothing to build L(x) from.

derivatives-in-context__dc-linearisation.√x is concave down. Is the linear estima: Too big — the tangent to a concave-down curve lies above it.

derivatives-in-context__dc-motion__mcq.At t = 2: v = −3 and a = 0. What is the: Moving backward at a steady speed, for that instant.

derivatives-in-context__dc-other-forms__.lim(x→0⁺) x·ln x is the indeterminate fo: Rewrite as (ln x)/(1/x) — now it is −∞/∞, which the rule handles.

derivatives-in-context__dc-related-rates.To find dA/dt when r = 3, a student writ: 9π is a constant, so its derivative is 0 — the substitution destroyed the very change being measured.

derivatives-in-context__dc-speed__mcq.v = −5 and a = −2. Is the particle speed: Speeding up — both are negative, so the acceleration pushes it further in the direction it is already going.
derivatives-in-context__dc-speed__mcq.v = 3(t − 1)(t − 3) and a = 6t − 12. Wha: Moving backward and SPEEDING UP — v < 0 and a < 0, the same sign.

differential-equations__de-equilibrium__.Solutions near y = 4 move TOWARD it from: y = 4 is stable (it attracts); y = 0 is unstable (it repels).

differential-equations__de-euler__mcq.Euler gives 2.25 where the true answer i: y = eˣ is concave UP, so every tangent step lies below the curve.

differential-equations__de-exponential__.Two samples of the same substance start: Neither — the half-life is the same. The y₀ cancels: T = ln2/k.

differential-equations__de-logistic__mcq.In dP/dt = kP(1 − P/K), what happens whe: The bracket is nearly 1, so dP/dt ≈ kP — it grows exponentially.
differential-equations__de-logistic__mcq.A logistic population sits between K/2 a: Still growing, but ever more slowly — easing toward the ceiling.

differential-equations__de-separable__mc.Separating dy/dx = 2xy required dividing: y = 0 — the equilibrium. Both sides are zero there, so it IS a solution, but dividing by y excluded it.

Match each equation to what its field lo.dy/dx = x: each COLUMN identical; steeper to the right
Match each equation to what its field lo.dy/dx = y: each ROW identical; steeper higher up

differential-equations__de-slope-field__.How many curves obey the instructions of: Infinitely many — one through every starting point. The initial condition picks one.
differential-equations__de-slope-field__.For dy/dx = 0.5y, what happens to the fi: The segments get STEEPER — the bigger y is, the faster it grows.

integration-accumulation__in-accumulatio.In A(x) = ∫₀ˣ f(t) dt, what is t?: A dummy variable — it sweeps across the interval and then disappears.

integration-accumulation__in-choosing-u_.For ∫ x²(x³ + 1)⁵ dx, what is u?: u = x³ + 1 — and du = 3x² dx, so x² dx = du/3.

integration-accumulation__in-constant-of.When does the + C actually matter?: For indefinite integrals — a definite integral subtracts it away.
integration-accumulation__in-constant-of.You know a tank's inflow rate for the wh: How much water was ADDED — but not how much is in the tank.

Match each part of ∫ₐᵇ f(x) dx to what i.∫: a stretched S — 'add them all up'
Match each part of ∫ₐᵇ f(x) dx to what i.dx: the WIDTH of a strip, shrunk to nothing

A(x) = ∫ₐˣ f has A′ = f, so A is an antiderivative of f (Part 1)
Any other antiderivative F differs from A by a constant
Constants cancel in a subtraction, so F(b) − F(a) = A(b) − A(a)
A(a) = 0, so A(b) − A(a) = A(b) = ∫ₐᵇ f

integration-accumulation__in-ftc1__mcq.How does d/dx[∫₅ˣ t³ dt] compare with d/: They are identical — both are x³. The lower limit only shifts A by a constant.

integration-accumulation__in-ftc2__mcq.Why can you use ANY antiderivative F whe: Two antiderivatives differ by a constant, and the constant cancels in F(b) − F(a).

integration-accumulation__in-library__mc.Why does ∫ x⁻¹ dx not follow the power r: The rule divides by n + 1, which is 0 when n = −1 — the formula breaks down.

integration-accumulation__in-net-change_.A runner goes forward, then back. ∫ v dt: She ended 2 miles from where she started, having run 8 miles in total.

integration-accumulation__in-read-accumu.f(x) = x − 2. Where is the accumulation: At x = 2, where f crosses zero from below.

integration-accumulation__in-riemann__mc.On a rising curve, why does the left-end: Each rectangle is only as tall as the LOWEST point of its strip, so it fits under the curve with room to spare.
integration-accumulation__in-riemann__mc.For f(x) = 2x (a straight line), which r: The trapezoid rule — a slanted top matches a straight line perfectly.

integration-accumulation__in-squeeze__mc.The gap between the left and right sums: h = (b − a)/n shrinks to 0, and the height difference is a fixed number.
integration-accumulation__in-squeeze__mc.For x² on [0, 2] with 2 strips, the left: The true area is somewhere between 1 and 5.

integration-accumulation__in-usub__mcq.In ∫ 2x(x² + 1)³ dx, what should u be?: u = x² + 1 — the inside of the bracket, whose derivative 2x is right there as a factor.

integration-applications__ia-area-betwee.On the interval (0, 1), which of y = x a: y = x — test x = 0.5: it gives 0.5 against 0.25.

integration-applications__ia-average-val.For f(x) = x² on [0, 3], the average of: The integral weights every x equally, and x² is LOW for most of the interval — so the true average is dragged down.

integration-applications__ia-cross-secti.The slices are equilateral TRIANGLES of: Only the constant: multiply the same ∫[f(x)]² dx by √3/4, the triangle's area coefficient.

integration-applications__ia-disc__mcq.A region under y = f(x) is revolved abou: f(x) — the height of the curve above the axis.
integration-applications__ia-disc__mcq.Which is the disc-method volume: π∫[f(x): π∫[f(x)]² dx — square the FUNCTION, then integrate.

Match each quantity to what you measure.Volume by discs: πr², with r the height of the curve

parametric-polar-calculus__pc-arc-length.What IS the quantity √((dx/dt)² + (dy/dt: The SPEED of the point — the magnitude of its velocity vector.

parametric-polar-calculus__pc-parametric.When does a parametric curve have a HORI: When dy/dt = 0 and dx/dt ≠ 0 — y has stopped moving while x carries on.

parametric-polar-calculus__pc-polar-area.Why does the polar area formula carry a: A thin wedge is a TRIANGLE, and a triangle's area is ½ · base · height.

parametric-polar-calculus__pc-vector-mot.A particle moves on the unit circle: r =: Yes — a = ⟨−cos t, −sin t⟩ has magnitude 1. The DIRECTION of the velocity keeps changing, even though its length does not.

series-convergence__sc-alternating__mcq.The partial sums of 1 − 1/2 + 1/3 − 1/4: Bouncing above and below, and closing in — each step is smaller than the last, so they squeeze onto a limit.

series-convergence__sc-comparison__mcq.Does Σ 1/(n² + 1) converge?: Yes — each term is smaller than 1/n², and Σ1/n² converges.
series-convergence__sc-comparison__mcq.A student says: 'Σ1/n² is smaller than t: Being smaller than a divergent series proves nothing — Σ1/n² is smaller, and it converges.
series-convergence__sc-comparison__mcq.Does Σ 1/(n − 1), from n = 2 onward, con: No — each term is BIGGER than 1/n, and the harmonic series diverges.

It diverges — you are adding lumps of a fixed size forever, so the pile can never settle.
series-convergence__sc-nth-term__mcq.The terms of 1 + 1/2 + 1/3 + 1/4 + … go: No — the harmonic series diverges, even though its terms fade to nothing.
series-convergence__sc-nth-term__mcq.Does Σ n/(n + 1) converge?: No — the terms tend to 1, not 0, so by the nth-term test it diverges.

series-convergence__sc-power-ops__mcq.To get a series for 1/(1 + x²), what do: Replace x with −x², giving 1 − x² + x⁴ − x⁶ + …

series-convergence__sc-radius__mcq.At x = 2, the series 1 + x + x² + … has: It gets WORSE — each term is bigger than the last, so the sum runs away.
series-convergence__sc-radius__mcq.For eˣ, the ratio of consecutive terms i: However big x is, the (n + 1) eventually outruns it — so the ratio goes to 0 for every x.

series-convergence__sc-ratio-test__mcq.Why does the ratio test work?: If |aₙ₊₁/aₙ| settles below 1, the tail eventually behaves like a geometric series with that ratio — and those converge.

series-convergence__sc-taylor__mcq.What are the first two terms of a Taylor: The tangent line at 0 — the linearisation from C2.
series-convergence__sc-taylor__mcq.Why does the xⁿ term carry a 1/n! ?: Differentiating xⁿ n times produces n!, so the 1/n! cancels it and makes the nth derivative come out right.
